results.title: interest rates essay (Maxim)
results.known: 24–25 out of 25, per the examiner (a real confirmed range, not a single invented number — deliberately kept as a range here rather than forced to one figure).

issues.text: The statement "interest rates only increase the cost of borrowing, does not therefore reduced disposable incomes of consumers" misrepresents the effect of higher rates on disposable income.

results.title: monopoly efficiency essay (Seb)
results.known: 21 out of 25, marked by his teacher (confirmed with George 2026-08-12 — not Seb's own self-assessment, which was the thing worth ruling out given Seb's interview describes him self-marking).

issues.text: The explanation of X‑inefficiency – "produce even AC and still make SNP (P−C×Q)" – is vague and does not clearly show why a monopoly can earn profit while operating above the efficient scale.

results.improvement: Clarify the X‑inefficiency argument by stating that a monopoly can set price above marginal cost, so even if it produces at a higher average cost than the efficient level it still earns a profit (SNP = (P‑C)×Q).

results.known: 19–20 out of 25, marked by the teacher (confirmed with George 2026-08-13). issues.text: The essay states "MPC is less than MSC" which incorrectly reverses the standard relationship between marginal private cost and marginal social cost.
